questions.q: Where does the dbt build actually fail first after raw_orders.status is renamed to order_status with no warning?
options: At the staging model, stg_jaffle_shop__orders — exactly one layer away from the raw source, with an invalid identifier error surfaced from Snowflake
In the Power BI report, with no error anywhere upstream
In the GitHub Actions workflow file itself
Nowhere — dbt silently ignores renamed columns
questions.explain: The staging model reads the old column name directly from source(), so it's the first and closest point of failure — exactly where Lesson 7 said a rename belongs.

questions.q: What does dbt ls --select stg_jaffle_shop__orders+ do, and why is it the real first move here?
options: It lists the model and everything downstream that depends on it, turning "what's the blast radius" into a graph query instead of a guess
It deletes the broken model so it can be rebuilt from scratch
It automatically fixes the broken column reference
It only works after the schema change has already been fixed
questions.explain: The + suffix selects the model and its downstream dependents, giving a precise, traceable list of every affected model via the ref()/source() graph.

questions.q: In the fix, why does the staging model's OUTPUT column stay named status even though the source column is now order_status?
options: Because Snowflake requires output column names to match input names
Because dbt does not allow renaming columns in a select statement
To contain the blast radius at exactly one file — every downstream model, test, and dashboard that already referenced status keeps working unmodified
It's arbitrary; renaming the output too would have made no difference
questions.explain: Renaming only the source-side read and keeping the staging model's own output name stable is what absorbs the change at one layer instead of rippling it everywhere.

questions.q: Which four stops does the fix for this schema change pass through, in order?
options: Power BI, CI/CD, Snowflake roles, then staging
Docs, then tests, then staging, then downstream SQL
Only the staging model needs to change; nothing else is affected
Staging, then any downstream SQL referencing the old name, then tests, then docs
questions.explain: The fix starts at staging (closest to the source), then checks downstream SQL, tests, and documentation for any other reference to the old column name.

questions.q: What would have happened if the staging model's output column had also been renamed to order_status, matching the source?
options: dbt would have automatically reverted the output name back to status
It would have made the fix faster with no downside
The rename would have rippled into every downstream model, every test, and the Power BI report, for a change that carries zero new information
Nothing different — renaming the output has no real effect
questions.explain: Letting the rename propagate past staging would force every consumer of status to change too — exactly what staging models exist to prevent.
